extracted.intended_audience: MER co-directors, Advisory Committee members, NSF program officers, and the mathematics education community
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating the effectiveness of the MER Forum (workshops, networks, newsletters, Advisory Committee) in supporting and facilitating mathematics education reform across K-12, undergraduate, and graduate levels using surveys, participant observation, and Advisory Committee feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop value to participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Most participants indicated that the workshops were valuable experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value manifested through opportunities to meet presenters and colleagues in informal settings, learning new information (often new to mathematician participants), and validation of participants' own educational notions and practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities for informal interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops should provide informal settings in which participants can meet presenters and colleagues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such face-to-face interactions are important for reducing isolation among mathematicians with educational interests and for facilitating communication and exchange of ideas; MER is effective largely because it facilitates these interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction of educational ideas into mathematics community
rubrics_metrics.description: MER should effectively bring educational ideas (even if not 'cutting edge' in education) into the mathematics world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even established education practices (e.g., cooperative learning, problem-solving pedagogy) can be novel to many mathematicians; success is judged by whether MER introduces these ideas to mathematicians who then adopt or consider them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling of reform-oriented pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop presenters should model less traditional, reform-oriented pedagogies (rather than only didactic approaches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants often want to maximize information in short workshops, so co-directors may need to intentionally encourage modeling of reform pedagogy (for example in afternoon breakout sessions) to balance information delivery and experiential demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee composition and role
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Committee members are chosen based on experience in education activities, leadership positions in the mathematics community, the K-12 community, and professional societies; the Committee advises co-directors but does not act in a policy-setting capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members bring their perspectives rather than gathering constituency feedback; evaluation should consider whether composition and meeting frequency allow for effective advising and whether additional structures (e.g., a Steering Committee) are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee meeting effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual Advisory Committee meetings should be productively organized to make limited face-to-face time count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given that the formal gathering may be brief, organizers should maximize productivity; informal dialogue across other MER events and electronic communication supplements the limited formal meeting time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee input on evaluation instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee should review and provide constructive feedback on evaluation instruments (e.g., surveys).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soliciting Committee feedback can materially improve instruments; the evaluation team received constructive comments which made the instruments better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of departmental network purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The departmental network must have a clearly articulated purpose (e.g., promoting educational reform that respects the integrity of mathematics) to guide dissemination and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion and design work are needed to determine what to disseminate and how; lack of clarity prolongs debate and can impede effective use of the network.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination strategy and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions must be made about what MER will disseminate and how dissemination will occur; major professional organizations (AMS & MAA) may be appropriate channels for publicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the two ways networks function: (1) push (newsletters pushing information) and (2) pull (providing descriptions and statistics so readers can pull pertinent data). Choose dissemination methods aligned with network intentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural indicators of support (workshops/newsletters)
rubrics_metrics.description: If MER is structurally supporting educational reform, there should be workshops or newsletters focused on targeted topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond structural mechanisms, participants should report spending time on educational initiatives and should value MER’s role; analysis of workshop topics over time can trace organizational emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of participant activities with MER's support
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants should be engaged in educational activities (classroom, outreach, curriculum/staff development, research) that align with MER’s vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure via participant self-reports (Not at all/A little/Considerably/Very) across domains (K-12, undergraduate curriculum, calculus reform, programs for pre-service/in-service teachers, efforts to increase participation of underrepresented groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate focus given limited resources
rubrics_metrics.description: MER should consider concentrating support where it can be most effective (e.g., undergraduate education) rather than trying to force broad K-12 participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than devoting entire workshops to less-popular pursuits, include K-12 portions within undergraduate workshops or create special interest groups for members focused on K-12 issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness in facilitating learning of new methods/materials
rubrics_metrics.description: MER should facilitate participants’ learning about new methods and materials they can use in their own classes and projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence includes participant reports of using others' ideas to expand efforts (e.g., teacher preparation, conceptual frameworks for reform) and instances where workshop talks helped solve practical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact on departmental legitimacy and administrative support
rubrics_metrics.description: MER should help participants make educational work more acceptable within their departments and provide evidence (e.g., peer institutions) to influence administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess participant reports that MER members influenced their administration or that MER improved their ability to cite peer institutions to administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to influence policy or state-level actors
rubrics_metrics.description: MER workshops should provide avenues to expose and influence state-level officials and educational policy (e.g., sponsoring attendance of state board officials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a state organization paid to send a state board official to a MER workshop; this was perceived as an effective mechanism to influence state policy actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding duplication with other organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether MER’s activities duplicate services available through other organizations (MAA, NCTM, AMS) and whether MER's unique reach justifies dedicated funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider MER’s uniqueness in reaching research mathematicians who do not participate in education organizations versus overlap in programming; weigh dissemination costs against impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for educational research vs service projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess MER’s role in supporting educational research: whether participants are engaged in research about teaching/learning or primarily service-type projects (curriculum development, in-service workshops).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The evaluation found little interest in conducting educational research; MER could consider offering sessions on methods for conducting educational evaluations to build capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitating collaboration within the mathematics community
rubrics_metrics.description: MER should effectively facilitate communication and collaboration among mathematicians about educational issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MER is unique in attracting research-oriented mathematicians to education discussions; evaluate whether MER brings together a distinct community and fosters productive exchanges among them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitating collaboration across professional communities
rubrics_metrics.description: MER should foster collaborations between mathematicians and mathematics educators (cross-community connections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current evidence shows limited communication and collaboration across communities; to build bridges, MER should invite more mathematics educators, present their research, and create workshop sessions that encourage cross-disciplinary exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mathematics education literature and avoiding 'recreating the wheel'
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematicians engaged in reform should consult mathematics education literature and educators rather than reinventing approaches by 'instinct alone.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less than half of mathematicians reported consulting educational research literature; MER could promote greater appreciation and use of education research to improve reform efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived credibility dynamics between mathematicians and educators
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants’ credibility as mathematics educators is often perceived to depend on their mathematics ability; this affects how education work is received within the mathematics community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize cultural status differences (research mathematicians valued highly) and consider how MER can mitigate barriers to valuing education expertise on its own terms.
